linkedin_post.hook: Why do Indians instantly reject adulterated milk, but happily drink chicory-blended coffee?
linkedin_post.body: A few months ago, sitting across from a veteran food technologist in Mumbai, I asked a simple question about consumer habits in the Indian market. We were dissecting the coffee consumption curve across Tier-1 and Tier-2 cities. He smiled, pointed at his black tea, and said something that completely shifted how I view our grocery shelves. 'Look at milk,' he said. 'The moment a packet smells slightly off or a brand is caught mixing water, consumers riot on social media. Sales plummet overnight. People demand complete transparency down to the fat percentage. But walk into a massive office pantry, pick up three popular instant coffee jars, and read the back. We have become fiercely protective of our proteins, our cold-pressed oils, and our organic pulses. Yet, when it comes to coffee—a daily ritual deeply tied to our morning focus and productivity—we have quietly accepted a diluted standard. We pay cafe prices for industrial fillers without ever turning the jar around to check the ingredient panel. The shift happening right now in the Indian coffee market isn't just about premiumisation. It is about a deeper awakening in workplace coffee culture and home brewing. People are starting to ask why health benefits of coffee are discussed everywhere, while the actual ingredient list is ignored. Real coffee consumption should mean single-origin beans, clean extraction, and zero hidden additives. Transparency shouldn't be a luxury feature reserved for specialty cafes. It should be the absolute baseline for every morning cup, whether you are fueling a high-stakes workday or enjoying a quiet Sunday morning. We need to start demanding the same ingredient honesty from our daily coffee that we already demand from every other item in our kitchen pantry.
